newsitem.title: UK: Eurobond activity slows ahead of U.S. jobs report.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond activity slows ahead of U.S. jobs report.

text.p: Primary market business slowed sharply on Friday morning as the wait for U.S. jobs data took its usual toll on financial market activity.

Structured deals accounted for the larger part of what new issues there were. Bankers Trust issued a callable subordinated three-year FRN and WestLB raised 1.0 billion marks via two deals, a five-year step-up and a four-year zero coupon.

A syndicate manager involved with the Bankers Trust deal said demand for broker-dealer paper had picked up since the recent merger of Dean Witter and Morgan Stanley. "Speculation about who is next has been a fillip for the market," he said.
Dealers said the BT issue, which pays three-month LIBOR plus 25 basis points, offered a 15 b.p. yield pick-up over an outstanding three-year senior deal.
"In the U.S. market you would only get a five pip pick-up at 10 years. So we think this is pretty generous pricing," the syndicate manager said.
Bear Stearns International and PaineWebber International were joint leads on the BT deal.
Elsewhere, the European Investment Bank launched a 1.0 trillion lire FRN in the Italian domestic market.
The EIB notes pay six-month LIBOR flat but are capped at 10 percent and have a step-up limit of 40 b.p. per coupon fixing.
